item.title: Tactus O1: First Based EVM Rollup on CKB (1 posts)
item.description: One canonical history. No privileged L2 sequencer. Following my earlier discussion on based EVM architectures for CKB, I’ve taken this direction forward as an independent project: Tactus O1. Tactus O1 is an experimental EVM validity rollup designed around CKB’s PoW consensus and Cell model. The central idea is to allow independent builders to propose EVM batches, while CKB determines their canonical succession and eventually verifies the resulting execution through validity proofs. I’m developing this as a solo research and engineering project for now. The repository already contains working components and reproducible experiments, although the complete rollup and its security guarantees...

item.title: Twine: Buy and Sell CKB Without Depositing on an Exchange (Fiber P2P PoC) (3 posts)
item.description: Nice write-up. I cloned the repo and read it end to end; the state machine is tidy and the tests are honest. One line of yours has been sitting with me: The operator can still settle or drop the preimage while the trade is open. That is the trust left in the coordinator. I’d fix that before deploying anything, because it turns out to be fixable with the RPCs you are already calling. item.description: Great to see FiberNuts continuing to evolve after the hackathon, I think the community market direction is a great way to demonstrate the value of combining Cashu with Fiber. item.title: [DIS] Hardening Kirea Finance (Native RWA Lending on CKB) (3 posts)
item.description: A small clarification for anyone reviewing this proposal: Kirea is not asking the DAO to fund an unbuilt RWA concept. The complete core lifecycle — RWA asset issuance, KYC attestation, deposit, borrow, repayment and release — is already implemented and verified on CKB testnet. The $7,250 request is specifically to harden that working pattern: generalize the asset/attestation components, integrate live KYC via Sumsub, handle repayment/default edge cases, and provide a reproducible testnet UI/tooling. item.title: Towards a Based EVM Layer on CKB: Three Architectural Options (1 posts)
item.description: Re-scoping: this direction will proceed as a separate project After reviewing how much of Myelin these designs would actually use, I want to correct the framing rather than let it stand. Here is the honest accounting on 9th Oct: The three options above need an EVM execution backend, an Ethereum state model and a new CKB-based sequencing protocol, none of which Myelin provides today. Direct code reuse would be limited to generic infrastructure: hashing primitives, a storage shell, the CKB follower adapter and some evidence-handling patterns.
